title: Daemon contract for honest contested holds: record_commit remedy text, get_commit_scope activeTaskIds
description:
Split from task-9d27749421b045c18a6c6eb99694236d along the daemon/wrapper seam (architect-e4b7eee0, 2026-10-30). That task keeps the wrapper half (moe-agent.{sh,ps1} held= remedy and label, postflight.{sh,ps1}, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) and depends on this one.

Objective. The MOE_CONTESTED_HELD alert tells every seat to release a skip-untouched hold by editing the path "with a wrapper-observed successful editing tool (Claude Edit/Write family or a supported Serena editor, not a shell write)". Only one-shot Claude stream-json sessions feed the wrapper's TOOL witness (docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Session touch evidence", docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md "Current witness limit"). A Codex, Gemini, Grok or interactive Claude seat that obeys stays held, and each round costs a QA reject (task-2cf1c6be and CQ-R11e2, 2026-10-30). Separately, held= names the peer entry's first claimant (taskIds[0]) even when an idle, dependency-gated task is first and a live one caused the hold (8f62fa0f named idle task-001d8ab3 while task-1e7f5a2d was live). The wrappers cannot fix that without per-task activity, which get_commit_scope does not serve today: peerActive is an OR over contributors.

Deliverable, packages/moe-daemon only plus docs/MCP_SERVER.md:
1. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.ts:
- HELD_REMEDY_UNTOUCHED names the three real release routes. Planned text: 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED: verify these bytes are this task\'s and coordinate any live peer. Before the next landing, either a one-shot Claude session of this task edits the path with a wrapper-observed successful editing tool (not a shell write), or a later session of this task that found the path clean at its pre-flight edits it while every contesting peer stays idle, or the stale peer task is legitimately completed or archived.'
- In HELD_REMEDY_EDITING, "either this task's own assignee session edits the path" becomes "either a one-shot Claude session of this task edits the path". The rest stays.
- New HELD_REMEDY_WITNESS, exactly: 'Only a one-shot (claude -p) Claude session\'s Edit/Write or Serena editing call leaves a TOOL witness; a Codex, Gemini, Grok or interactive Claude session\'s edits, Serena\'s included, leave none.' It is appended after the editing remedy whenever the line has an untouched or editing hold, before the strict remedy and the never-clause. task-9d277494's wrappers reuse this exact sentence in their held= remedy, so keep it byte-stable.
- Unchanged: HELD_REMEDY_STRICT, HELD_REMEDY_NEVER, hold classification, peer naming, the 5-path bound and the #governors rate limit.
2. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts: each peerDeclared entry gains activeTaskIds: string[]. It lists the contributing tasks that are active by the peerActive rule, in id order; without `since`, that is every contributor.
- Invariants: editingTaskIds is a subset of activeTaskIds, and peerActive === (activeTaskIds.length > 0).
- Update the tool description string beside taskIds/editingTaskIds.
- The field is additive. A wrapper that predates it ignores it. task-9d277494's wrappers read it to name editing, then active, peers before idle claimants. An absent field counts as [].
3. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.test.ts and getCommitScope.test.ts: exact-string and shape tests (see DoD).
4. docs/MCP_SERVER.md:
- In the get_commit_scope Returns block, add activeTaskIds to the peerDeclared type and its comment.
- Update the record_commit "Held contested paths" bullets to the new remedy text. The EDITING bullet quotes its line verbatim, so update the quote too. Name the witness sentence and when it is appended.

NOT in scope:
- Any wrapper or harness file (task-9d277494).
- Codex `--json` witness harvest (the split sibling filed with this row).
- Which paths are held or landed, record_commit's classification or rate limits.
- docs/roles/governor.md.

Verification: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npm test`. activeTaskIds is an additive wire field on a wrapper-facing tool, so this runs the full daemon suite, not one file.
definitionOfDone: recordCommit.test.ts asserts the exact new lines. An untouched-only hold reads `... — <HELD_REMEDY_UNTOUCHED> <HELD_REMEDY_WITNESS> <HELD_REMEDY_NEVER>`, and an editing hold has the witness sentence after the editing remedy. Neither line contains 'Claude Edit/Write family or a supported Serena editor' or 'this task\'s own assignee session edits'.
A strict-only (MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED) MOE_CONTESTED_HELD line is byte-identical to before this change, without the witness sentence, proven by an exact-string recordCommit.test.ts case.

get_commit_scope peerDeclared entries carry activeTaskIds, proven by new getCommitScope.test.ts cases. With `since`, an idle first contributor and an active second give taskIds [first, second], activeTaskIds [second] and peerActive true. Without `since`, every contributor is listed. editingTaskIds is a subset of activeTaskIds in every case.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md documents activeTaskIds in the get_commit_scope Returns block, and the record_commit held-path bullets match the new constants, quoted verbatim where the doc quotes.
`cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npm test` passes.

implementationPlan.description:
get_commit_scope activeTaskIds, TESTS FIRST. Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts, then packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts.

1. Tests, red first.
   - ScopeResult's peerDeclared type gains activeTaskIds: string[].
   - Three existing whole-entry toEqual assertions gain the field, since toEqual fails on an unlisted key:
     - 'ORs over every task contributing a path': activeTaskIds [activeId];
     - the task-66e8/task-9cc1 test: ['task-9cc1'] on both entries;
     - 'lists a task once per path': ['task-a', 'task-b'].
   - New describe('peerDeclared[].activeTaskIds'):
     - T1 (the DoD case), with since: an idle first contributor (unassigned, no attempt) and an active second (assignee worker-live, lastActivityAt now) on one path. The entry toEqual { path, taskId: <first>, peerActive: true, taskIds: [first, second], activeTaskIds: [second], editingTaskIds: [] }.
     - T2, with since, every contributor idle: activeTaskIds [] and peerActive false.
     - T3, without since: two contributors (one unassigned, one with a missing worker). activeTaskIds equals taskIds: every contributor is listed.
     - T4, with since: an idle IN_PROGRESS contributor sorting first and an active IN_PROGRESS one. taskIds is [idle, active], and activeTaskIds and editingTaskIds are both [active].
     - T5, a helper expectActiveInvariants(result). For every entry it checks: activeTaskIds is a subset of taskIds in the same order; editingTaskIds is a subset of activeTaskIds; peerActive === (activeTaskIds.length > 0). Call it in every test of the 'peerDeclared[].peerActive' and 'taskIds and editingTaskIds' describes, so it also covers the open, quiet, slack, late, stale and corrupt attempt rows, the waits-on-this rule and junk step data.
     - T6: getCommitScopeTool(h.state).description contains 'activeTaskIds'.
   Red: cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\packages\moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts" fails T1-T6 and the three updated assertions on today's code. Record it.
2. Implementation, getCommitScope.ts only.
   - In the peer loop, the entry type gains activeTaskIds: string[], placed between taskIds and editingTaskIds.
   - A new entry gets activeTaskIds: active ? [other.id] : []. An existing entry pushes other.id when active.
   - Tasks are visited in id order and each contributes a path once, so the order is id order. editing is computed only when active, so the subset and peerActive invariants hold by construction. Do not add a second activity rule.
   - Update the loop's comment and the tool description string beside taskIds/editingTaskIds: activeTaskIds lists the contributors active by the peerActive rule, in id order (every contributor without `since`); editingTaskIds is a subset of it; peerActive is true exactly when it is non-empty.
3. Green: the same command passes. The top-level reply-keys test stays unchanged, because the field is nested.

Error handling: unchanged. Junk peer records still never fail the scope (existing junk-data tests, now with T5's invariants).
